speaker: Doctor
text: I need to ask a few more questions to narrow this down. Has the pain radiated to your back or groin, and do you notice any blood in your urine? Also, have you had any recent fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) with possible concurrent Urinary Tract Infection. The combination of dysuria, dyspareunia, pelvic pain, nausea, and vomiting in a sexually active young woman is highly suggestive of PID. I recommend a urine pregnancy test, NAAT for Chlamydia/Gonorrhea, and a pelvic ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis and rule out ectopic pregnancy or tubo-ovarian abscess.
